claim: IL-12 drives the generation of terminally differentiated KLRG1+ effector CD8+ T cells.
source: The proinflammatory cytokine IL-12 drives the generation of terminally differentiated KLRG1+ effector CD8+ T cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a primary finding of the study.

claim: Direct IL-12 signaling on CD8+ T cells is essential for the induction of KLRG1.
source: We demonstrate that direct IL-12 signaling on CD8+ T cells is essential for the induction of KLRG1 and IFN-γ, but the subsequent downregulation of CXCR3 is controlled by IL-12 indirectly through the actions of IFN-γ and IFN-γ-inducible chemokines.
evidence: Demonstrated through adoptive transfer experiments with IL-12rβ2 deficient cells (Figure 5).

claim: Direct IL-12 signaling on CD8+ T cells is essential for the induction of IFN-γ.
source: We demonstrate that direct IL-12 signaling on CD8+ T cells is essential for the induction of KLRG1 and IFN-γ, but the subsequent downregulation of CXCR3 is controlled by IL-12 indirectly through the actions of IFN-γ and IFN-γ-inducible chemokines.
evidence: Demonstrated through adoptive transfer experiments with IL-12rβ2 deficient cells (Figure 5).

claim: The downregulation of CXCR3 is controlled by IL-12 indirectly through the actions of IFN-γ and IFN-γ-inducible chemokines.
source: We demonstrate that direct IL-12 signaling on CD8+ T cells is essential for the induction of KLRG1 and IFN-γ, but the subsequent downregulation of CXCR3 is controlled by IL-12 indirectly through the actions of IFN-γ and IFN-γ-inducible chemokines.
evidence: Demonstrated through neutralization experiments and in vitro assays (Figures 6, 7).

claim: Differentiation of nascent effectors occurs in an extrafollicular splenic compartment.
source: Differentiation of nascent effectors occurs in an extrafollicular splenic compartment and is driven by late IL-12 production by DCs distinct from the classical CD8α+ DC.
evidence: Demonstrated using intravascular staining methods (Figure 3) and immunohistochemistry (Figure 8).

claim: Late IL-12 production by DCs distinct from the classical CD8α+ DC drives differentiation of nascent effectors.
source: Differentiation of nascent effectors occurs in an extrafollicular splenic compartment and is driven by late IL-12 production by DCs distinct from the classical CD8α+ DC.
evidence: Demonstrated through intracellular cytokine staining showing CD11c+ CD11b+ myeloid DCs produce IL-12 at day 3 (Figure 7C).

claim: There is extensive proliferation of both KLRG1− and KLRG1+ CD8+ T cells in the marginal zone and red pulp.
source: Unexpectedly, we also found extensive proliferation of both KLRG1− and KLRG1+ CD8+ T cells in the marginal zone and red pulp, which ceases prior to the final KLRG1Hi CXCR3Lo stage.
evidence: Demonstrated through EdU labeling and immunohistochemistry (Figure 8).

claim: Proliferation of CD8+ T cells ceases prior to the final KLRG1Hi CXCR3Lo stage.
source: Unexpectedly, we also found extensive proliferation of both KLRG1− and KLRG1+ CD8+ T cells in the marginal zone and red pulp, which ceases prior to the final KLRG1Hi CXCR3Lo stage.
evidence: Demonstrated through EdU labeling showing CXCR3 downregulation occurs in non-proliferating KLRG1+ CD8+ T cells (Figure 8G).

claim: The activation of naïve CD8+ T cells occurs in the T cell areas of secondary lymphoid organs.
source: The activation of naïve CD8+ T cells occurs in the T cell areas of secondary lymphoid organs (Mempel et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Once activated, CD8+ T cells undergo rapid clonal expansion and differentiate into IFN-γ-producing effector cytotoxic lymphoid cells through an 'autopilot' mechanism.
source: Once activated, CD8+ T cells are thought to undergo rapid clonal expansion and differentiate into IFN-γ-producing effector cytotoxic lymphoid cells (CTLs) through an 'autopilot' mechanism (Mercado et al., 2000; Bevan and Fink, 2001; Kaech and Ahmed, 2001; van Stipdonk et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a statement of existing paradigm supported by multiple citations.

claim: CD8α+ dendritic cells are critical for antigen cross-presentation.
source: Consistent with this paradigm, CD8α+ dendritic cells (DCs), which are resident in the splenic white pulp, are critical for both antigen cross-presentation (den Haan et al., 2000) and production of a key pro-inflammatory cytokine, IL-12 (Reis e Sousa et al., 1997; Mashayekhi et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work.

claim: CD8α+ dendritic cells are critical for production of IL-12.
source: Consistent with this paradigm, CD8α+ dendritic cells (DCs), which are resident in the splenic white pulp, are critical for both antigen cross-presentation (den Haan et al., 2000) and production of a key pro-inflammatory cytokine, IL-12 (Reis e Sousa et al., 1997; Mashayekhi et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: IL-12 is an important signal 3 cytokine that drives clonal proliferation of activated CD8+ T cells in vitro.
source: IL-12 is an important signal 3 cytokine that drives clonal proliferation of activated CD8+ T cells in vitro (Curtsinger et al., 1999) as well as their effector cytokine production in vivo (Schmidt and Mescher, 1999, 2002; Valenzuela et al., 2002; Liu et al., 2006; Wilson et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work.

claim: IL-12 drives effector cytokine production by CD8+ T cells in vivo.
source: IL-12 is an important signal 3 cytokine that drives clonal proliferation of activated CD8+ T cells in vitro (Curtsinger et al., 1999) as well as their effector cytokine production in vivo (Schmidt and Mescher, 1999, 2002; Valenzuela et al., 2002; Liu et al., 2006; Wilson et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Following their activation and migration into the inner PALS, CD8α+ DCs become hyporesponsive and cease IL-12 production.
source: However, following their activation and migration into the inner PALS (Reis e Sousa et al., 1997), CD8α+ DCs become hyporesponsive and cease IL-12 production (Reis e Sousa et al., 1999), raising the question of whether this initial early burst of IL-12 is sufficient to drive end-stage effector CD8+ T cell differentiation to completion.
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: CXCR3 deficiency results in an inefficient generation of cytokine-producing effector cells and instead favors a response skewed towards memory cells.
source: CXCR3 deficiency results in an inefficient generation of cytokine-producing effector cells and instead favors a response skewed towards memory cells (Kohlmeier et al., 2011; Kurachi et al., 2011; Groom et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: CXCR3 is essential for secondary effector T cell generation from central memory T cells.
source: The role of CXCR3 in lymphocyte peripheralization also extends to the memory response and is essential for secondary effector T cell generation from central memory T cells (Sung et al., 2012; Kastenmuller et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: IL-12 potently promotes CD8+ T cell effector differentiation and function through T-bet-dependent induction of KLRG1 expression and IFN-γ production.
source: In particular, the cytokine IL-12 potently promotes CD8+ T cell effector differentiation and function, through T-bet-dependent induction of KLRG1 expression and IFN-γ production (Joshi et al., 2007; Wilson et al., 2008, 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: IL-12 appears to control the migratory potential of primary and effector T cells by negatively regulating CXCR3 expression.
source: In addition to these effects, IL-12 appears to also control the migratory potential of primary and effector T cells, by negatively regulating CXCR3 expression (Slutter et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work.

claim: There is little change in absolute cell numbers of tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells between day 0 and day 4 post-vaccination in the spleen.
source: Figure 1A shows that there is little change in absolute cell numbers of tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells between day 0 and day 4 post-vaccination in the spleen.
evidence: Shown in Figure 1A with quantification of tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells over time.

claim: A 10-fold clonal expansion occurs between days 4 and 5 post-infection in spleens of both WT and IL-12 deficient mice.
source: However, we can detect a 10-fold clonal expansion occurring between days 4 and 5-post infection in spleens of both WT and IL-12 deficient mice.
evidence: Shown in Figure 1A with quantification of tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells over time.

claim: The absolute numbers of tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells continue to increase at similar rates through day 7 in WT and IL-12 deficient mice.
source: The absolute numbers of tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells continue to increase at similar rates through day 7 in WT and IL-12 deficient mice.
evidence: Shown in Figure 1A with quantification of tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells over time.

claim: The lack of IL-12 signals does not affect the timing or the magnitude of the proliferative response of tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells during T. gondii vaccination.
source: These results indicate that the lack of IL-12 signals does not affect the timing or the magnitude of the proliferative response of tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells during T. gondii vaccination.
evidence: Inferred from the data in Figure 1A showing similar expansion kinetics in WT and IL-12p35−/− mice.

claim: By day 3, approximately 7-8% of the tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells start to commit to putative TEM and TEFF cells by downregulating CD62L and increasing KLRG1 expression in WT hosts.
source: However, by day 3, ∼7–8% of the tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells start to commit to putative TEM and TEFF cells by downregulating CD62L and increasing KLRG1 expression in the WT hosts (Figure 1B).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1B pie charts showing stage distribution over time.

claim: In IL-12p35 deficient hosts, L-selectin downregulation is observed starting on day 3, however KLRG1 upregulation is absent.
source: In IL-12p35 deficient hosts, L-selectin downregulation is also observed starting on day 3, however KLRG1 upregulation is absent (Figure 1B).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1B pie charts comparing WT and IL-12p35−/− mice.

claim: On day 4, there is a dramatic increase in the frequency of tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells that have downregulated CD62L, a third of which also acquire KLRG1 in WT mice.
source: On day 4, there is a dramatic increase in the frequency of tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells that have downregulated CD62L, a third of which also acquire KLRG1 in WT mice.
evidence: Shown in Figure 1B pie charts showing stage distribution at day 4.

claim: In the absence of IL-12, there is an attenuation of KLRG1 expression resulting in a larger frequency of F2 tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells.
source: However, in the absence of IL-12, there is an attenuation of KLRG1 expression resulting in an even larger frequency of F2 tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1B pie charts comparing WT and IL-12p35−/− mice at day 4.

claim: The frequency of KLRG1+ tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells continues to increase through day 7 post-vaccination in WT hosts.
source: The frequency of KLRG1+ tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells continues to increase through day 7 post-vaccination in WT hosts; yet, in IL-12 deficient mice, KLRG1 upregulation remains attenuated and the frequencies of F3 stage tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells do not reach levels seen WT hosts (Figure 1B).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1B pie charts showing stage distribution through day 7.

claim: In IL-12 deficient mice, KLRG1 upregulation remains attenuated and the frequencies of F3 stage tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells do not reach levels seen in WT hosts.
source: The frequency of KLRG1+ tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells continues to increase through day 7 post-vaccination in WT hosts; yet, in IL-12 deficient mice, KLRG1 upregulation remains attenuated and the frequencies of F3 stage tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells do not reach levels seen WT hosts (Figure 1B).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1B pie charts comparing WT and IL-12p35−/− mice through day 7.

claim: IL-12 signaling has an important role on the differentiation of KLRG1+ effector tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells, and this occurs earlier than the proliferative burst seen after day 4.
source: These results indicate that IL-12 signaling has an important role on the differentiation of KLRG1+ effector tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells, and that this occurs earlier than the proliferative burst seen after day 4.
evidence: Inferred from the data showing KLRG1 upregulation starting at day 3 while proliferative burst occurs between days 4-5.

claim: Downregulation of CD62L and subsequent clonal expansion are IL-12 independent.
source: In contrast, downregulation of CD62L and subsequent clonal expansion are IL-12 independent.
evidence: Inferred from data showing similar CD62L downregulation and expansion kinetics in WT and IL-12p35−/− mice (Figure 1).

claim: The absolute numbers of tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells in the PECs in an IL-12 deficient environment by day 6 were attenuated by one log in absolute numbers.
source: Surprisingly, we found that the absolute numbers of tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells in the PECs in an IL-12 deficient environment by day 6 were attenuated by one log in absolute numbers as the height of the adaptive immune response was reached (Figure 1C).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1C with quantification of tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells in PECs.

claim: T-bet is a master regulator of the differentiation and functional activity of effector CD8+ T cells.
source: The T-box protein, T-bet, is a master regulator of the differentiation and functional activity of effector CD8+ T cells.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in the field.

claim: T-bet associates with the promoters of genes for KLRG1.
source: It has been shown to associate with the promoters of genes for KLRG1 (Joshi et al., 2007), IFN-γ (Joshi et al., 2007), as well as the chemokine receptor, CXCR3 (Beima et al., 2006; Harms Pritchard et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: T-bet associates with the promoters of genes for IFN-γ.
source: It has been shown to associate with the promoters of genes for KLRG1 (Joshi et al., 2007), IFN-γ (Joshi et al., 2007), as well as the chemokine receptor, CXCR3 (Beima et al., 2006; Harms Pritchard et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: T-bet associates with the promoters of genes for CXCR3.
source: It has been shown to associate with the promoters of genes for KLRG1 (Joshi et al., 2007), IFN-γ (Joshi et al., 2007), as well as the chemokine receptor, CXCR3 (Beima et al., 2006; Harms Pritchard et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: CXCR3 expression is highly expressed when CD8+ T cells are CD62L+ or CD62L−.
source: Analysis of CXCR3 expression as CD8+ T cells differentiate from F1 (TCM) to F2 (TEM) cells in the spleen show that CXCR3 expression is highly expressed when CD8+ T cells are CD62L+ or CD62L− (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: Shown in Figure 2A,B with flow cytometry analysis of CXCR3 expression.

claim: The early expression of CXCR3 is IL-12 independent, but T-bet dependent.
source: Interestingly, our data demonstrate that the early expression of CXCR3 is IL-12 independent, but T-bet dependent (Figure 2A,B) and as these cells differentiate into end-stage effector IFN-γ producing KLRG1+ CD8+ T cells, they downregulate CXCR3 (Figure 2A,B), indicating that IL-12 has late downregulatory effects on CXCR3 expression.
evidence: Shown in Figure 2A,B comparing CXCR3 expression in WT, IL-12p35−/−, and Tbx21−/− mice.

claim: As CD8+ T cells differentiate into end-stage effector IFN-γ producing KLRG1+ CD8+ T cells, they downregulate CXCR3.
source: Interestingly, our data demonstrate that the early expression of CXCR3 is IL-12 independent, but T-bet dependent (Figure 2A,B) and as these cells differentiate into end-stage effector IFN-γ producing KLRG1+ CD8+ T cells, they downregulate CXCR3 (Figure 2A,B), indicating that IL-12 has late downregulatory effects on CXCR3 expression.
evidence: Shown in Figure 2A,B with flow cytometry analysis of CXCR3 expression across differentiation stages.

claim: IL-12 has late downregulatory effects on CXCR3 expression.
source: Interestingly, our data demonstrate that the early expression of CXCR3 is IL-12 independent, but T-bet dependent (Figure 2A,B) and as these cells differentiate into end-stage effector IFN-γ producing KLRG1+ CD8+ T cells, they downregulate CXCR3 (Figure 2A,B), indicating that IL-12 has late downregulatory effects on CXCR3 expression.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that CXCR3 downregulation occurs in KLRG1+ cells and is IL-12 dependent.

claim: On day 4, tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells upregulate KLRG1 expression after trafficking to the RP.
source: Interestingly, our results suggest that on day 4, tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells upregulate KLRG1 expression after trafficking to the RP (Figure 3B).
evidence: Shown in Figure 3B using intravascular staining to distinguish white pulp and RP localization.

claim: By day 7 post-vaccination, the tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells are found to be equally localized to the white pulp and the RP prior to increasing their KLRG1 expression.
source: By day 7 post-vaccination, the tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells are found to be equally localized to the white pulp and the RP prior to increasing their KLRG1 expression, where, once KLRG1 expression is upregulated, the majority (∼80%) of the cells is located in the RP.
evidence: Shown in Figure 3B with quantification of RP distribution by differentiation stage.

claim: Once KLRG1 expression is upregulated, the majority (approximately 80%) of the cells is located in the RP.
source: By day 7 post-vaccination, the tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells are found to be equally localized to the white pulp and the RP prior to increasing their KLRG1 expression, where, once KLRG1 expression is upregulated, the majority (∼80%) of the cells is located in the RP.
evidence: Shown in Figure 3B with quantification of RP distribution by differentiation stage.

claim: The early upregulation of KLRG1 expression on tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells occurs mainly in the RP.
source: Thus, the early upregulation of KLRG1 expression on tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells occurs mainly in the RP, where they may be encountering a secondary signal of the pro-inflammatory cytokine, IL-12, for later differentiation into end-stage effector CD8+ T cells.
evidence: Inferred from the data showing preferential RP localization of KLRG1+ cells (Figure 3B).

claim: At day 4, CXCR3 expression in both KLRG1− and KLRG1+ CD8+ T cells is not substantially decreased.
source: As Figure 3C indicates, at day 4 CXCR3 expression in both KLRG1− and KLRG1+ CD8+ T cells is not substantially decreased, but by day 7, the KLRG1+ CD8+ T cells which are predominantly RP-localized have completely downregulated CXCR3.
evidence: Shown in Figure 3C with quantification of CXCR3 expression on KLRG1− and KLRG1+ cells.

claim: By day 7, the KLRG1+ CD8+ T cells which are predominantly RP-localized have completely downregulated CXCR3.
source: As Figure 3C indicates, at day 4 CXCR3 expression in both KLRG1− and KLRG1+ CD8+ T cells is not substantially decreased, but by day 7, the KLRG1+ CD8+ T cells which are predominantly RP-localized have completely downregulated CXCR3.
evidence: Shown in Figure 3C with quantification of CXCR3 expression on KLRG1+ cells at day 7.

claim: Prior to the upregulation of KLRG1, effector precursor CD8+ T cells expressing high levels of CXCR3 can migrate to the RP, where they upregulate KLRG1 and then downregulate CXCR3 as they differentiate into late-stage effector CD8+ T cells.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrate that prior to the upregulation of KLRG1, effector precursor CD8+ T cells expressing high levels of CXCR3 can migrate to the RP, where they upregulate KLRG1 and then downregulate CXCR3 as they differentiate into late-stage effector CD8+ T cells.
evidence: Inferred from the temporal and spatial data showing CXCR3 expression, KLRG1 upregulation, and RP localization (Figure 3).

claim: The blockade of IL-12 at early, late or both time points did not affect absolute tgd057-specific CTL numbers.
source: Consistent with our earlier results, the blockade of IL-12 at early, late or both time points did not affect absolute tgd057-specific CTL numbers (Figure 4A).
evidence: Shown in Figure 4A with quantification of tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells after IL-12 neutralization at different time points.

claim: When IL-12 is neutralized only on day 3, KLRG1 expression and IFN-γ-production were still attenuated, albeit less markedly compared to the effects of early and continuous blockade of the cytokine.
source: When IL-12 is neutralized only on day 3, KLRG1 expression and IFN-γ-production were still attenuated, albeit less markedly compared to the effects of early and continuous blockade of the cytokine (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: Shown in Figure 4B,C with analysis of KLRG1 expression and IFN-γ production after IL-12 neutralization at different time points.

claim: Late neutralization of IL-12 interrupts the downregulation of CXCR3 expression on late-stage effector tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells.
source: Importantly, we find that late neutralization of IL-12 interrupts the downregulation of CXCR3 expression on late-stage effector tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells (Figure 4D).
evidence: Shown in Figure 4D with analysis of CXCR3 expression after IL-12 neutralization at different time points.

claim: IL-12 is required for early programming of effector differentiation.
source: These results confirm that IL-12 is required for early programming of effector differentiation, and indicate that IL-12 production occurs days after initial CPS vaccine exposure and continues to induce further differentiation of effector-fated CD8+ T cells.
evidence: Inferred from the neutralization experiments showing effects of early IL-12 blockade (Figure 4).

claim: IL-12 production occurs days after initial CPS vaccine exposure and continues to induce further differentiation of effector-fated CD8+ T cells.
source: These results confirm that IL-12 is required for early programming of effector differentiation, and indicate that IL-12 production occurs days after initial CPS vaccine exposure and continues to induce further differentiation of effector-fated CD8+ T cells.
evidence: Inferred from the neutralization experiments showing effects of late IL-12 blockade (Figure 4).

claim: The lack of IL-12 signaling does not alter the frequency of IL-12rβ2 deficient donor CD8+ T cells.
source: 7 days after CPS-vaccination, we observe that the lack of IL-12 signaling does not alter the frequency of IL-12rβ2 deficient donor CD8+ T cells (Figure 5B), but CXCR3 downregulation is inhibited (Figure 5C).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5B with analysis of donor cell frequencies in adoptive transfer experiments.

claim: The lack of IL-12 signaling inhibits CXCR3 downregulation.
source: 7 days after CPS-vaccination, we observe that the lack of IL-12 signaling does not alter the frequency of IL-12rβ2 deficient donor CD8+ T cells (Figure 5B), but CXCR3 downregulation is inhibited (Figure 5C).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5C with analysis of CXCR3 expression in adoptive transfer experiments.

claim: IL-12 is not essential for T cell expansion in vivo.
source: These results confirm earlier conclusions that IL-12 is not essential for T cell expansion in vivo and are consistent with the notion that IL-12 directly signals the downregulation of CXCR3 expression.
evidence: Inferred from the adoptive transfer experiments showing similar frequencies of WT and IL-12rβ2−/− donor cells (Figure 5B).

claim: The F3 stage KLRG1+ CD8+ T cells had downregulated CXCR3 regardless of their ability to signal IL-12.
source: However, when we further compared CXCR3 expression between KLRG1− vs KLRG1+ stages, we found that the F3 stage KLRG1+ CD8+ T cells had downregulated CXCR3 regardless of their ability to signal IL-12 (Figure 5D).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5D with analysis of CXCR3 expression in KLRG1+ cells from WT and IL-12rβ2−/− donors.

claim: CXCR3 is downregulated in a non-CD8+ T cell autonomous manner.
source: We conclude that CXCR3 is downregulated in a non-CD8+ T cell autonomous manner, which is not consistent with previous results (Slutter et al., 2013).
evidence: Inferred from the adoptive transfer experiments showing CXCR3 downregulation in KLRG1+ cells regardless of IL-12 receptor expression (Figure 5D).

claim: The apparent lack of CXCR3 downregulation is due to the predominant deficiency in KLRG1 expression on the IL-12Rβ2 deficient CD8+ T cells.
source: The apparent lack of CXCR3 downregulation is due to the predominant deficiency in KLRG1 expression on the IL-12Rβ2 deficient CD8+ T cells (Figure 5E).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5E with analysis of stage distribution in WT and IL-12rβ2−/− donor cells.

claim: KLRG1 expression behaves in a cell autonomous manner.
source: Unlike CXCR3, KLRG1 expression and IFN-γ production, that are known to be directly regulated by IL-12 signaling, behave in a cell autonomous manner (Figure 5E,F).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5E,F with analysis of KLRG1 expression and IFN-γ production in WT and IL-12rβ2−/− donor cells.

claim: IFN-γ production behaves in a cell autonomous manner.
source: Unlike CXCR3, KLRG1 expression and IFN-γ production, that are known to be directly regulated by IL-12 signaling, behave in a cell autonomous manner (Figure 5E,F).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5E,F with analysis of IFN-γ production in WT and IL-12rβ2−/− donor cells.

claim: In vivo blockade of IFN-γ as late as D3 disrupts the downregulation of CXCR3 expression in KLRG1-expressing tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells.
source: We found that in vivo blockade of IFN-γ as late as D3 disrupts the downregulation of CXCR3 expression in KLRG1-expressing tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells (Figure 6A) without attenuating KLRG1 upregulation or IFN-γ production (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: Shown in Figure 6A with analysis of CXCR3 expression after IFN-γ neutralization.

claim: IFN-γ neutralization does not attenuate KLRG1 upregulation or IFN-γ production.
source: We found that in vivo blockade of IFN-γ as late as D3 disrupts the downregulation of CXCR3 expression in KLRG1-expressing tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells (Figure 6A) without attenuating KLRG1 upregulation or IFN-γ production (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: Shown in Figure 6B,C with analysis of KLRG1 expression and IFN-γ production after IFN-γ neutralization.

claim: The addition of IFN-γ maintains the low levels of CXCR3 on CD8+ T cells, to a similar extent as the addition of IL-12.
source: As expected, the addition of IP-10 rapidly decreases the expression of CXCR3 on CD8+ T cells lacking IL-12 signals (Figure 7A, left), but importantly, the addition of IFN-γ and not the addition of CXCL10 alone, maintains the low levels of CXCR3 on these CD8+ T cells, to a similar extent as the addition of IL-12 (Figure 7A, right).
evidence: Shown in Figure 7A with in vitro assays measuring CXCR3 expression after cytokine/chemokine treatment.

claim: IFN-γ can act directly on the CD8+ T cell to suppress CXCR3 expression.
source: Consistent with this notion, addition of IFN-γ alone to highly purified CD8α+ TCRβ+ T cells from D7 CPS vaccinated IL-12p35 deficient spleens still maintains the low levels of CXCR3 expression (Figure 7B) without the need for IL-12-producing accessory cells, indicating that IFN-γ can act directly on the CD8+ T cell.
evidence: Shown in Figure 7B with in vitro assays on purified CD8+ T cells.

claim: CD11c+ CD11b+ DCs (myeloid DCs), but not CD8α+ DCs produced IL-12 at day 3 post-CPS vaccination.
source: CD11c+ CD11b+ DCs (myeloid DCs [mDCs]), but not CD8α+ DCs produced IL-12 (Figure 7C, D3).
evidence: Shown in Figure 7C with intracellular cytokine staining of splenocytes from D3 CPS vaccinated mice.

claim: There is late production of IL-12 by a subset of mDCs distinct from the CD8α+ DCs known to be the primary producers of IL-12 during early T. gondii infection.
source: This result confirms that there is late production of IL-12 by a subset of mDCs distinct from the CD8α+ DCs known to be the primary producers of IL-12 during early T. gondii infection (Figure 7C, 4 hr).
evidence: Shown in Figure 7C comparing IL-12 production at 4 hr vs D3 post-vaccination.

claim: CD4+ and CD8+ T cells are producing IFN-γ in the spleen on day 3.
source: We also found that CD4+ and CD8+ T cells (Figure 7D), and to a much lesser extent NK cells, are producing IFN-γ in the spleen on day 3, suggesting that these cell types are putatively responding to the IL-12 derived from these myeloid APCs.
evidence: Shown in Figure 7D with intracellular cytokine staining for IFN-γ in different cell types.

claim: The same myeloid APC subsets producing IL-12 are also the same cells producing CXCL9 and CXCL10.
source: Finally, we find that the same myeloid APC subsets producing IL-12 are also the same cells producing CXCL9 and CXCL10 (Figure 7C) presumably in response to the IFN-γ derived from TH1 CD4+ and CD8+ T cells.
evidence: Shown in Figure 7C with intracellular staining for IL-12, CXCL9, and CXCL10 in DC subsets.

claim: Nearly all of the IL-12/chemokine-positive DCs on D3 are CCR2+.
source: Indeed, nearly all of the IL-12/chemokine -positive DCs on D3 are CCR2+ (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A with analysis of CCR2 expression on IL-12/chemokine-producing DCs.

claim: Transient ablation of CCR2+ monocytes/derivatives resulted in markedly diminished KLRG1+ (F3 and F4) subpopulations.
source: Transient ablation resulted in markedly diminished KLRG1+ (F3 and F4) subpopulations and attenuation in CXCR3 downregulation in the KLRG1+ CD8+ T cells.
evidence: Shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B,C with analysis of CD8+ T cells in CCR2-DTR mice after diphtheria toxin treatment.

claim: Transient ablation of CCR2+ monocytes/derivatives resulted in attenuation in CXCR3 downregulation in the KLRG1+ CD8+ T cells.
source: Transient ablation resulted in markedly diminished KLRG1+ (F3 and F4) subpopulations and attenuation in CXCR3 downregulation in the KLRG1+ CD8+ T cells.
evidence: Shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B,C with analysis of CD8+ T cells in CCR2-DTR mice after diphtheria toxin treatment.

claim: A significantly greater proportion of proliferating CD8+ T cells (labeled within a narrow 2 hr period) were localized to the RP.
source: We found that a significantly greater proportion of proliferating CD8+ T cells (labeled within a narrow 2 hr period) were localized to the RP (Figure 8A, left) and comprised predominantly of CD62L− CD8+ T cells (F2 and F3) (Figure 8A, right).
evidence: Shown in Figure 8A with EdU labeling and intravascular staining to localize proliferating cells.

claim: Proliferating CD8+ T cells comprised predominantly of CD62L− CD8+ T cells (F2 and F3).
source: We found that a significantly greater proportion of proliferating CD8+ T cells (labeled within a narrow 2 hr period) were localized to the RP (Figure 8A, left) and comprised predominantly of CD62L− CD8+ T cells (F2 and F3) (Figure 8A, right).
evidence: Shown in Figure 8A with EdU labeling and analysis of differentiation stages.

claim: On a per cell basis, the proliferative rate increases as cells progress from F1 to F3 stages.
source: In fact, on a per cell basis, the proliferative rate increases as cells progress from F1 to F3 stages (Figure 8B, left) and exhibit the same skewed extrafollicular localization of cycling CD62L− CD8+ T cells (Figure 8B, right).
evidence: Shown in Figure 8B with analysis of EdU incorporation rates across differentiation stages.

claim: Cycling CD62L− CD8+ T cells exhibit skewed extrafollicular localization.
source: In fact, on a per cell basis, the proliferative rate increases as cells progress from F1 to F3 stages (Figure 8B, left) and exhibit the same skewed extrafollicular localization of cycling CD62L− CD8+ T cells (Figure 8B, right).
evidence: Shown in Figure 8B with analysis of RP localization of EdU+ cells by differentiation stage.

claim: EdU-positive cells double-labeled with IV injected anti-CD8α and ex vivo stained anti-CD8α antibodies are readily observed in the MZ.
source: As shown in Figure 8E, EdU-positive cells double-labeled with IV injected anti-CD8α and ex vivo stained anti-CD8α antibodies are readily observed in the MZ (marked with yellow arrows in Figure 8E) and in bridging channels (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Shown in Figure 8E with immunofluorescence imaging of spleen sections.

claim: EdU-positive cells double-labeled with IV injected anti-CD8α and ex vivo stained anti-CD8α antibodies are readily observed in bridging channels.
source: As shown in Figure 8E, EdU-positive cells double-labeled with IV injected anti-CD8α and ex vivo stained anti-CD8α antibodies are readily observed in the MZ (marked with yellow arrows in Figure 8E) and in bridging channels (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1 with immunofluorescence imaging of spleen sections.

claim: Extrafollicular proliferative CD8+ T cells are observed in the RP, many of which are also KLRG1+.
source: Extrafollicular proliferative CD8+ T cells are also observed in the RP, many of which are also KLRG1+ (marked with pink arrows in Figure 8F).
evidence: Shown in Figure 8F with immunofluorescence imaging showing EdU+ KLRG1+ CD8+ T cells in RP.

claim: Clonal proliferation does not cease when CD8+ T cells acquire the effector cell marker, KLRG1.
source: Interestingly, these data also indicate that clonal proliferation does not cease when CD8+ T cells acquire the effector cell marker, KLRG1.
evidence: Inferred from the observation of EdU+ KLRG1+ cells (Figure 8F).

claim: CXCR3 downregulation is observed in non-proliferating KLRG1+ CD8+ T cells.
source: As Figure 8G indicates, CXCR3 downregulation is observed in non-proliferating KLRG1+ CD8+ T cells.
evidence: Shown in Figure 8G with analysis of CXCR3 expression in EdU− vs EdU+ KLRG1+ cells.

claim: CD8+ T cell proliferation is not restricted to the T cell area.
source: These results indicate that, unlike the predominant view, CD8+ T cell proliferation is not restricted to the T cell area.
evidence: Inferred from the data showing extensive proliferation in the RP and MZ (Figure 8).

claim: Upon activation, CD44 is rapidly upregulated and then L-selectin (CD62L) is downregulated in an IL-12-independent manner.
source: Upon activation, CD44, a surface receptor necessary for T cell adhesion to extracellular matrix proteoglycans, is rapidly upregulated and then L-selectin (CD62L) is downregulated in an IL-12-independent manner (Figure 1).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1 with analysis of CD44 and CD62L expression in WT and IL-12p35−/− mice.

claim: CXCR3 is expressed early in the CD44Hi, CD62L+ (F1) CD8+ T cell stage, and remains highly expressed through the CD44Hi, CD62L− (F2) CD8+ T cell stage.
source: CXCR3 is expressed early in the CD44Hi, CD62L+ (F1) CD8+ T cell stage, and remains highly expressed through the CD44Hi, CD62L− (F2) CD8+ T cell stage (Figure 2).
evidence: Shown in Figure 2 with analysis of CXCR3 expression across differentiation stages.

claim: While still in the white pulp and even prior to CD8+ T cell expansion, a few CD44Hi, CD62L− CD8+ T cells begin to acquire KLRG1 surface expression in an IL-12 dependent manner.
source: While still in the white pulp and even prior to CD8+ T cell expansion (Figures 1, 3), a few CD44Hi, CD62L− CD8+ T cells begin to acquire KLRG1 surface expression in an IL-12 dependent manner.
evidence: Shown in Figures 1 and 3 with analysis of KLRG1 expression and localization.

claim: As CD8+ T cell numbers increase and outmigrate to the RP, KLRG1 expression escalates.
source: As CD8+ T cell numbers increase and outmigrate to the RP, KLRG1 expression escalates (Figure 3).
evidence: Shown in Figure 3 with analysis of KLRG1 expression and RP localization over time.

claim: Most of the proliferating CD8+ T cells are CD62L− (F2 and F3 stage CD8+ T cells) and many of these cycling effector precursors are observed to be outmigrating into the MZ via bridging channels.
source: Unexpectedly, we found that most of the proliferating CD8+ T cells are CD62L− (F2 and F3 stage CD8+ T cells) and many of these cycling effector precursors are observed to be outmigrating into the MZ (Figure 8) via bridging channels (Figure 8—figure supplement 1) (Khanna et al., 2007).
evidence: Shown in Figure 8 and Figure 8—figure supplement 1 with EdU labeling and immunofluorescence imaging.

claim: Extrafollicular KLRG1+ precursor effector CD8+ T cells downregulate CXCR3 expression in an IL-12 dependent fashion.
source: Finally, these extrafollicular KLRG1+ precursor effector CD8+ T cells downregulate CXCR3 expression in an IL-12 dependent fashion.
evidence: Inferred from the data showing CXCR3 downregulation in RP-localized KLRG1+ cells and the requirement for IL-12 (Figures 3, 4).

claim: CXCR3 downregulation by IL-12 is indirectly mediated by IFN-γ and IFN-γ-dependent chemokines, which are produced by other T lymphocytes and mDCs, respectively.
source: CXCR3 downregulation by IL-12 is indirectly mediated by IFN-γ and IFN-γ-dependent chemokines, which are produced by other T lymphocytes and mDCs, respectively (Figure 7), in the MZ where the extrafollicular CD8+ T cells have been shown to cluster and interact with inflammatory myeloid cells producing IL-12 in a CXCR3 dependent manner (Kurachi et al., 2011).
evidence: Shown in Figure 7 with analysis of cytokine and chemokine production by different cell types.

claim: Extrafollicular CD8+ T cells cluster and interact with inflammatory myeloid cells producing IL-12 in a CXCR3 dependent manner in the MZ.
source: CXCR3 downregulation by IL-12 is indirectly mediated by IFN-γ and IFN-γ-dependent chemokines, which are produced by other T lymphocytes and mDCs, respectively (Figure 7), in the MZ where the extrafollicular CD8+ T cells have been shown to cluster and interact with inflammatory myeloid cells producing IL-12 in a CXCR3 dependent manner (Kurachi et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The tetramer-based enrichment method allows for a approximately 2-log increase in detection of tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells.
source: The tetramer-based enrichment method allows for a ∼2-log increase in detection of tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells (Figure1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 comparing pre- and post-enrichment detection.

claim: There are 2093 ± 273 endogenous tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells in spleens of naïve WT mice.
source: We are able to detect 2093 ± 273 and 1200 ± 138 endogenous tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells in spleens of naïve WT and IL-12p35 deficient mice, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 with quantification using SCNT spike-in method.

claim: There are 1200 ± 138 endogenous tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells in spleens of naïve IL-12p35 deficient mice.
source: We are able to detect 2093 ± 273 and 1200 ± 138 endogenous tgd057-specific CD8+ T cells in spleens of naïve WT and IL-12p35 deficient mice, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 with quantification using SCNT spike-in method.

claim: The findings argue against the notion that effector CTL generation occurs through an 'autopilot' sequence.
source: Taken together with earlier studies (Lauvau et al., 2001; Cockburn et al., 2010), our findings argue against the notion that effector CTL generation occurs through an 'autopilot' sequence and, instead, involves a multi-leveled progression of effector T cell precursors through distinct splenic microenvironments, where their differentiation is controlled by a complex interplay with locally positioned activated immune cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings in the context of previous work.

claim: Effector CTL generation involves a multi-leveled progression of effector T cell precursors through distinct splenic microenvironments, where their differentiation is controlled by a complex interplay with locally positioned activated immune cells.
source: Taken together with earlier studies (Lauvau et al., 2001; Cockburn et al., 2010), our findings argue against the notion that effector CTL generation occurs through an 'autopilot' sequence and, instead, involves a multi-leveled progression of effector T cell precursors through distinct splenic microenvironments, where their differentiation is controlled by a complex interplay with locally positioned activated immune cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings in the context of previous work.

claim: The findings highlight the notion of an extrafollicular pathway for effector T cell generation.
source: Our findings highlight the notion of an extrafollicular pathway for effector T cell generation.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main finding of the study.

claim: There is an analogous and well-recognized extrafollicular differentiation pathway of IgG class switched plasma cells producing the primary antibody response to T cell-dependent antigens in the B cell response.
source: Interestingly, in the B cell response, there is an analogous and well-recognized extrafollicular differentiation pathway of IgG class switched plasma cells producing the primary antibody response to T cell-dependent antigens (MacLennan et al., 2003; Kurosaki et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The non-germinal center plasma cell response is favored by strong B cell receptor signaling and antigen presentation by MZ localized DCs.
source: By analogy to the way that the non-germinal center plasma cell response is favored by strong B cell receptor signaling and antigen presentation by MZ localized DCs (Paus et al., 2006; Phan et al., 2006; Chappell et al., 2012), the extrafollicular generation of effector CD8+ T cells is also likely regulated by differential T cell receptor signaling (Bernhard et al., 2015) and local cytokine and chemokine milieu created by specialized pathogen-engaged APCs interacting with bystander lymphocytes in the MZ and RP.
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The extrafollicular generation of effector CD8+ T cells is likely regulated by differential T cell receptor signaling and local cytokine and chemokine milieu created by specialized pathogen-engaged APCs interacting with bystander lymphocytes in the MZ and RP.
source: By analogy to the way that the non-germinal center plasma cell response is favored by strong B cell receptor signaling and antigen presentation by MZ localized DCs (Paus et al., 2006; Phan et al., 2006; Chappell et al., 2012), the extrafollicular generation of effector CD8+ T cells is also likely regulated by differential T cell receptor signaling (Bernhard et al., 2015) and local cytokine and chemokine milieu created by specialized pathogen-engaged APCs interacting with bystander lymphocytes in the MZ and RP.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on analogy to B cell responses and supported by citations.

claim: The exposure of effector precursors to the extrafollicular tissue niche could provide major extrinsic factors that determine the observed interclonal and intraclonal variability in effector lymphocyte fates that is independent of their intrinsic TCR-peptide:MHC affinity and dwell time.
source: The exposure of effector precursors to this extrafollicular tissue niche could provide major extrinsic factors that determine the observed interclonal and, perhaps, intraclonal variability in effector lymphocyte fates that is independent of their intrinsic TCR-peptide:MHC affinity and dwell time (Plumlee et al., 2013; Tubo et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the implications of the findings, supported by citations.
